subject: Preserving logs during incident — data retention & hold request
messages:
From: Samir Joshi <samir@chroniclehealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@chroniclehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Preserving logs during incident — data retention & hold request

Hi Vivek / Monica,

We discovered potential data exposure related to a subset of test traffic on our integration and our legal team has opened an investigation. We need Redwood to preserve certain logs while the investigation is open. Specifically:

- Retain admin/audit logs for the Chronicle account (org-level admin actions, key rotations, user role changes) for the last 12 months and continue retention going forward until the hold is lifted.
- Preserve API request metadata (request_id, timestamp, model id, response metadata) for the period 2026-06-01 through 2026-10-01.

Questions:
1) What are Redwood's default retention windows for audit logs and API request logs today?
2) Can you suspend automatic deletion for the specified ranges and grant an account-level retention hold?
3) If we need a longer retention window (24 months), what is the process, approvals needed, and any cost/contract implications?

We attached a legal hold notification from our counsel. Please confirm receipt and next steps. This is time sensitive — please respond within EOD PT.

Attachment: cust_legal_hold_notice.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks,
Samir Joshi
Director, IT Security
Chronicle Health
samir@chroniclehealth.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Joshi <samir@chroniclehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-10T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Preserving logs during incident — data retention & hold request

Hi Samir — thanks for flagging and for the legal notice. I’ve looped in Monica (CS) and Naomi (Security) so we can coordinate next steps. Below is a concise summary of our defaults and the options for an account-level hold.

Summary of Redwood default retention (prod platform):
- Audit & security logs (auth events, admin actions, config changes): 365 days.
- API request metadata (request_id, model, token counts, timing metrics — excluding full prompt/response content): 90 days.
- Application-level request traces and embeddings are retained by default for 30 days; model cache/KV are ephemeral and not considered part of persistent logs.

What we can do for Chronicle now:
- Suspend scheduled deletion jobs for the account for the narrow scopes you requested (org audit logs and the API request metadata for the specified date range).
- We can implement an account-level retention exception to extend retention to 24 months for the agreed log types, but this requires:
  1) A signed retention-exception form (attached).
  2) Approval from Security (Naomi) and sign-off from Finance for storage surcharge.
  3) A short contract amendment/PO so we can track billing and legal terms.

Notes & constraints:
- By default we do not preserve prompt/response content (requests/responses that include PII) unless Chronicle explicitly requests a Data Export under the Data Subject / Export process and provides redaction instructions.
- We will scope the exception narrowly (exact log types and date ranges). We avoid open-ended indefinite holds because of storage and compliance considerations.
- Exports can be provided in CSV/NDJSON and delivered to a secure transfer location (SFTP or encrypted Drive link); this is the recommended path for legal investigations.

Action items:
- Monica: please work with Samir to complete the attached cust_retention_exception_form.pdf and confirm billing contact.
- Naomi: can you review for security implications and list any gating checks before we flip the suspension switch?
- Samir: if you can confirm the exact range and whether you require prompt/response content (and provide redaction expectations), we’ll prepare the exception and cost estimate.

I’ve attached a short retention_policy_summary.pdf that maps policy to log categories. Will follow up once we have the signed form.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai
Attachment: retention_policy_summary.pdf (application/pdf)

Vivek / Monica — quick security review and recommendation: 

- We are comfortable approving a timeboxed retention exception for Chronicle limited to:
  • Org audit logs (auth, admin actions, API key activity, role changes)
  • API request metadata (request_id, timestamps, model id, token counts, latency)
  • Delivery: export-as-needed or preserve in-platform under the exception flag

- Recommended retention window: 24 months from the approval date (i.e., 2026-10-11 through 2028-10-11).
- We must explicitly exclude full prompt/response payloads containing PII unless Chronicle signs the Data Export redaction agreement and provides redaction criteria.
- Operational considerations: engineering needs 48 business hours to change deletion jobs and ensure retention markers are applied; we should schedule a maintenance window if bulk exports are requested.
- Security gating: confirm the list of admin emails that can request lift of the hold; require 2-person approval (Chronicle legal + Redwood security) to lift.

Action items for internal triage:
1) Monica — confirm billing contact and route the exception form to Legal/Procurement for contract amendment.
2) Vivek — confirm final scope with customer and get signed cust_retention_exception_form.pdf.
3) Naomi/Security — will validate deletion job pause and monitor for any unexpected data access.

I’m OK to sign off once we have the completed form and billing PO.

— Naomi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Preserving logs during incident — data retention & hold request

Samir — thanks for the patience. Confirming Redwood will implement the requested preservation and a 24-month retention exception for the agreed scopes once we have the signed paperwork:

Scope (approved):
- Org audit logs: auth events, admin actions, API key operations, role changes (all accounts under Chronicle org).
- API request metadata for 2026-06-01 through present: request_id, timestamps, model id, token counts, latency, status codes.

What we will NOT preserve without explicit request:
- Full prompt/response bodies containing user content or PII (those require a separate Data Export/redaction agreement).
- Transient KV cache and model internal checkpoints — these are ephemeral and not recorded in retention logs.

Operational details and timeline: 
- We will suspend deletion jobs for the specified scope and tag retained objects with an exception flag. Engineering will apply the flags within 48 business hours of receiving the signed exception form.
- Retention window: 24 months from 2026-10-11 (exception expiry date 2028-10-11).
- Exports: we can produce NDJSON/CSV exports on request; provide secure SFTP endpoint or allow Redwood to place files in your approved drive.
- Cost: Finance will add a storage surcharge to cover the extended retention; Monica will share the estimate and PO process.

Next steps (for you):
1) Please sign and return the attached cust_retention_exception_form.pdf.
2) Confirm whether you need full prompt/response exports (and, if yes, provide redaction guidance).
3) Provide billing contact for invoicing the surcharge.

I’ve attached the signed exception form we’ll use to track approvals; once we have the signed copy and PO, Naomi’s team will flip the switch and Engineering will apply the retention markers.

Attachment: signed_exception_form.pdf (application/pdf)

If you want, we can set a 30-minute call today to go over the mechanics and export options.

Best regards,
